summary: HomelabOS is a self-hosting solution designed to help you run an offline, privacy-centric data centre on your own hardware. It uses Docker to let you deploy a large collection of over one hundred distinct services with a minimal set of commands. The project is distributed under the MIT licence and provides a structured way to manage multiple self-hosted applications simultaneously.
goodFor: This is well-suited for technical users who want to quickly spin up a wide variety of self-hosted services without configuring each container individually from scratch.
watchOut: The repository currently shows a complete lack of recent commits, which indicates that development may be stalled and you might encounter unpatched bugs or outdated service configurations.
deployNotes: Because the project relies entirely on Docker, you will typically need to ensure persistent storage volumes are configured for your containers and manage your own reverse proxy for TLS termination.
